item.title: TideGrab 0.9.1
item.description:
Open pages that need more

  • Open Page in TideGrab: when a link needs a sign-in or a site can't be read, open the page in TideGrab, sign in if it asks, press play, and add what it plays.
  • Sign-ins are kept per site inside TideGrab and sent only to that site. Settings › Browser lists them and signs out.

Convert saved files

  • Convert… to MP4 (H.264 or HEVC, HDR kept), ProRes, GIF, M4A, MP3, FLAC or WAV, with size, quality and an optional part.
  • TideGrab says what converting costs before it starts, and points to the copy without re-encoding when that gives the same result.
  • Save Audio As MP3, M4A, FLAC or WAV. Downloads can also save audio as FLAC or WAV.
  • Frame previews and trimming for every format, WebM and MKV included.

Better names

  • Links queued together get their real titles and thumbnails.
  • File names read naturally: "Film: Part 2" saves as "Film - Part 2".

TideGrab Pro

  • Lists and playlists, several downloads at once, Convert, live recording, Follow, Shortcuts, the browser extension and media-library names are TideGrab Pro (€19.99 once). Until Pro goes on sale, all of it is included.

Updates

  • TideGrab now updates itself. Settings › Updates checks once a day and installs signed updates when you quit.

Changes

  • "Use my browser's sign-in" and the aria2 option are gone; Open Page replaces the first.
  • Sites that block download tools (such as Rumble and Bilibili) now say so plainly.
  • The list view's selected row and the shortcut hints are easier to read.
  • The window no longer scrolls: a long playlist's list makes room, and only the queue scrolls.
  • The browser extension ships inside the app: Browser Extension… › Show Extension Folder.

item.title: TideGrab 0.9.2
item.description:
Made for audio

  • Sound-only links (music, mixes, radio shows, podcasts) get their own choices: Original, exactly as the site sends it, or M4A, MP3, FLAC or WAV for that download. Each choice says whether it's a straight copy or a re-encode, and FLAC or WAV made from a compressed stream says it can't sound better than the stream.
  • The artist's own file: when an artist allows downloads, sign in to the site once in Open Page and TideGrab saves the file they uploaded, often lossless, instead of the compressed stream.
  • Tags: artist, album and track number, filled in from the page and editable before you save. Cover art goes into the file.
  • The card shows what the sound is before you download it: format, bitrate, sample rate and channels.

Trim, front and centre

  • Trim… is at the top of every saved item's menu, on the hover bar of each tile, and on ⌘T.
  • Sound files get a real waveform with handles, a playhead and Listen from here.
  • Skip silence at the ends moves the handles to where the sound starts and stops.
  • On the confirmation card, Trim to keeps only part of a video or recording before it downloads.

Convert, with sound tools

  • A loudness meter: integrated loudness (EBU R128), true peak and loudness range.
  • Even out the loudness, fade in and fade out.
  • Advanced: a loudness target (Streaming −14, Podcast −16 or Broadcast −23 LUFS, measured on the part you keep, peaks under −1 dBTP), sample rate, bit depth (16-bit dithered or 24-bit) and channels.
  • Check the Sound… shows a spectrogram and says whether a FLAC or WAV looks like it was made from a compressed file.

item.title: TideGrab 0.9.3
item.description:
Changes

  • The dotted arrow on the start screen and in Welcome now fades out in a soft circle. Its ripples no longer stop at a square edge.

item.title: TideGrab 0.9.4
item.description:
Changes

  • The dotted arrow on the start screen and in Welcome is symmetric again: it sits exactly on the dot grid at any window size.

item.title: TideGrab 0.9.5
item.description:
Changes

  • When a link needs its page: a link TideGrab can't read on its own (it needs a sign-in, or the site turns direct requests away) now gets a clear next step instead of an error. TideGrab says why in one line, then Open the Page lets you sign in if the site asks, press play, and add the video.
  • In the downloads list, those items say the same calmly, with Open the Page as the main button.

item.title: TideGrab 0.9.6
item.description:
Fixes

  • Videos that wouldn't open: many videos failed with "The helper returned more data than expected". Their sites now list subtitles in about 150 languages, which made a single video's details over 10 MB. TideGrab now reads them.
  • Report… keeps the part of a link that names the video (such as `?v=`), so a report no longer arrives as a bare ".../watch". Private tokens and share keys are still left out.

item.title: TideGrab 0.9.7
item.description:
Select several at once

  • ⌘-click adds or removes an item, Shift-click selects a range, and ⌘A (or Edit › Select All) selects everything shown. Esc lets go.
  • With several selected, a bar offers Remove from List, Show in Finder and Save Audio As for all of them. Right-click a selected item for the same.

Sound

  • Edit Sound… (⌘E, or the waveform button on a tile) for saved music and recordings: loudness, fades, skip silence and the Advanced options, on the file's own format. Save Audio As no longer lists the type a file already is.
  • A video saved as audio gets the same choices as a music link: M4A, MP3, FLAC or WAV (each says whether it's a copy or a re-encode), tags, and the video's thumbnail as cover art.
  • Videos get Even out the loudness and fades in Convert; only the sound is re-encoded.

List view

  • The list fills the window, however short it is.
  • Gallery | List is now in the top right of the window, in both views, with the row size next to it in List.
  • Larger row sizes show bigger posters.

Fixes

  • Mixcloud and similar sites: downloads no longer fail at the end when the site's best stream can't hold cover art.
  • AV1 videos (YouTube in 4K, on Macs before M3): Trim and Convert now show frames instead of loading forever. TideGrab's ffmpeg now includes dav1d.
  • Drop a link on the menu bar icon to download it.

item.title: TideGrab 0.9.8
item.description:
Intel Macs

  • TideGrab now runs natively on Intel Macs as well as Apple silicon (macOS 15 or later). One download works on both.
  • Its ffmpeg and deno helpers are universal too, so conversions, previews and site support work the same on either Mac.
